If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1–2% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast downward by 1–3% in the 10–15 day window to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) across 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1% downward bias to late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overfitting to recent trends.  
If sentiment is positive but recent prices are trending downward, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1% for mid horizon to align with momentum reversal.  
If sentiment is negative but recent prices are trending upward, increase forecast slope by 0.5–1% for early horizon to capture sentiment-driven reversal.
